response.title: Do I really need a special screen for a projector that sits right under the picture, or can I just use a white wall or a regular screen?
response.answer:
You don't absolutely need a special screen, but for a projector that sits directly below the image, a special screen can make a huge difference.

That type of projector is called an ultra-short-throw (UST) projector. It projects light upward at a steep angle, which makes it more sensitive to the projection surface than a normal projector.

Here's how your options compare:

1. White wall — works, with limitations

You can absolutely use a white wall. In a dark room, the picture can look quite good. But even slight wall texture or unevenness can create visible shadows and distortion.

Shop

2. Regular projector screen — sometimes works

A smooth, flat, matte-white screen can work well. However, many retractable screens aren't perfectly flat, and UST projectors exaggerate every ripple. Avoid conventional ALR screens designed for long-throw projectors.

Shop

3. UST ALR/CLR screen — best performance

These screens are specifically designed to reflect light coming from below toward your eyes while rejecting much of the light coming from above. They produce much better contrast in rooms with ambient light.

What I'd recommend

Your situation

	

Best choice




Dark room, budget-conscious

	

Smooth white wall




Dark room, want better image flatness

UST-specific ALR/CLR screen

One important distinction: UST screens aren't just expensive regular screens. Their optical surface is directional, so using the wrong ALR screen can actually make the picture worse.

Two questions that would change my recommendation:

What projector do you have (brand/model)?

Will you mostly watch in a dark room, or a living room with lights/windows?

Depending on those answers, you might be able to save several hundred dollars by skipping the specialized screen without sacrificing much picture quality.
